items.title: Ray Vega interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 20, 2023
items.q: You put down “Blues and the Abstract Truth” Oliver Nelson.

ctx.x: Well what happens is these kids are also getting on the Internet and getting tons of information and getting there’s — I think it’s sensory overload, the amount of information that they can get. So I slow them down and I just tell them okay, let’s slow down and I let them know, you know, you’re going to have to learn how to play by ear. You’re going to have to. I tell them you’ve got to learn all these scales, you’re going to learn all these patterns, you’re going to get the sound of this under your fingers. When…

together for these Blue Note sessions which they really just — these were not working bands. They got together, looked at the music and went in. But at that point they were speaking to each other in such a highly sophisticated fashion that they could hear through things. They could hear through things. So what I tell the students is I tell them you’re not going to be able to play freely if all you’re going to have is that piece of music in front of you and looking at the chord progressions to figure out what you…

remember going down to 24th Street and they had an interesting loft apartment, it was a great apartment. I remember getting up there and he had like an old school stereo system, you know a real nice sounding stereo, and he’d put that recording on of Dexter Gordon’s “Sophisticated Giant” and we just sat there, Pablo and myself I think. Pablo Carey teaches in Maine. Another one of our buds in those circles was David Glasser who plays lead alto with the Basie band. So we’d be sitting there going oh wow, and…
